info.name: Expense Claims API
info.description: Auth and claim endpoints. Import the matching environment, set its `password` (the seed password), run '1. Auth' first, then '2. Claims' in order. Every error has { error: { code, message, requestId, details? } }.

exec: // Today's date (UTC) for line item dates: they must not be in the future

request.description: Liveness check used by Docker and load balancers. Needs no token and is not logged.
Saves the JWT in {{token}}. Run this first. Needs the `password` environment variable.

exec: pm.test("Response has a token and the user", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("claimantEmail")); });

request.description: Saves a second claimant's token in {{tokenOther}}, used by the isolation checks.

exec: pm.test("Response has a token and the user", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("claimant2Email")); });

request.description: Saves an approver's token in {{tokenApprover}}, used by the role checks.

exec: pm.test("Response has a token and the user", function () { pm.expect(body.token).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(body.user.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("approverEmail")); });

pm.test("Returns the logged-in user without a password hash", function () { const u = pm.response.json().user; pm.expect(u.email).to.eql(pm.variables.get("claimantEmail")); pm.expect(u).to.not.have.property("passwordHash"); });

request.description: Saves {{claimId}} and {{itemId}} (the first line item) for the next requests. The total is computed by the server; sending `total` is rejected.

exec: pm.test("Draft with a computed total of 30.50", function () { pm.expect(claim.status).to.eql("DRAFT"); pm.expect(claim.total).to.eql("30.50"); pm.expect(claim.lineItems.length).to.eql(2); });

item.name: Create claim with no items (empty draft)

request.description: Saves {{emptyClaimId}}: the 'Delete' request below removes THIS draft, so the main test claim survives for the line item requests.

exec: pm.test("Total is 0.00 with no items", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("0.00"); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(0); });

pm.test("Has data and pagination, no line items in the list", function () { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.data).to.be.an("array"); pm.expect(b.pagination).to.have.all.keys("page","pageSize","totalItems","totalPages"); if (b.data.length) { pm.expect(b.data[0]).to.have.property("lineItemCount"); pm.expect(b.data[0]).to.not.have.property("lineItems"); } });
pm.test("Same claim with its items", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("claimId")); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("30.50"); });

request.description: Only the title can be edited (the total is derived, the status follows the workflow). Works on any claim except an APPROVED one; a title change leaves the total unchanged, so an approval chain is not reset.

exec: pm.test("Title changed, total and items untouched", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.title).to.eql("Postman test claim (renamed)"); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("30.50"); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(2); pm.expect(c.status).to.eql("DRAFT"); });

item.name: Delete a claim (DELETE, the empty draft)

request.description: Only a DRAFT can be deleted. A submitted claim (pending, rejected or approved) is part of the audit trail and returns 409.
The body is ONE line item. The date uses {{today}}, which a collection pre-request script sets.

exec: pm.test("Total went up by 7.25 (30.50 -> 37.75), 3 items", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("37.75"); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(3); });

item.name: Update a line item: only the amount (PATCH)

request.description: PATCH changes only the fields you send (at least one of date, category, amount, description). This example sends just the amount; the next request changes several fields.

exec: pm.test("Total is now 45.25 (the 12.50 item became 20.00)", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().total).to.eql("45.25"); });

item.name: Update a line item: several fields at once (PATCH)

request.description: Any combination of date, category, amount and description. Fields you leave out stay as they are.

exec: pm.test("Total unchanged (45.25): the amount was not touched", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().total).to.eql("45.25"); });

pm.test("Description, category and date changed together", function () { const item = pm.response.json().lineItems.find(i => i.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("itemId")); pm.expect(item.description).to.eql("Team lunch"); pm.expect(item.category).to.eql("TRAVEL"); pm.expect(item.date).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("today")); pm.expect(item.amount).to.eql("20.00"); });

pm.test("Item is gone and total recomputed (45.25 - 20.00 = 25.25)", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("25.25"); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(2); pm.expect(c.lineItems.map(i => i.id)).to.not.include(pm.collectionVariables.get("itemId")); });

request.description: Uses {{claimId}} from the claims folders (it still has line items). The server builds the approval chain from the total: level 1 approver PENDING, higher levels WAITING.

exec: pm.test("Now pending approval, submittedAt set, total is a string", function () { pm.expect(claim.status).to.eql("PENDING_APPROVAL"); pm.expect(claim.submittedAt).to.not.eql(null); pm.expect(claim.total).to.be.a("string"); });

request.description: Only a DRAFT can be submitted; a double click or retry is refused.

item.name: Rename the submitted claim -> 200 (title only, total unchanged)

request.description: A claim awaiting approval can be edited. A title change does not change the total, so the approval chain is NOT reset.

exec: pm.test("Still pending, title changed, total unchanged", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.status).to.eql("PENDING_APPROVAL"); pm.expect(c.title).to.eql("Postman test claim (renamed while pending)"); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("submitTotal")); });

item.name: Change an item's amount on the submitted claim -> 200 (chain reset)

request.description: The total changes, so every approval so far is void and the chain restarts from level 1 (same approvers, new chainVersion; two history rows: CLAIM_UPDATED and APPROVAL_CHAIN_RESET). No endpoint shows approvals yet, so this request checks the new total.

exec: pm.test("Still pending, new amount and a different total", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.status).to.eql("PENDING_APPROVAL"); const item = c.lineItems.find(function (i) { return i.id === pm.collectionVariables.get("submitItemId"); }); pm.expect(item.amount).to.eql("777.77"); pm.expect(c.total).to.not.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("submitTotal")); });

request.description: A submitted claim is part of the audit trail and is never deleted.

item.name: Create an empty draft for the submit check

request.description: Saves {{emptyDraftId}}: a draft with no line items.

item.name: Submit a claim with no line items -> 422 NO_LINE_ITEMS
Create a one-item claim (for the last-item rule)

request.description: Saves {{oneItemClaimId}} and {{oneItemId}}.
A claim awaiting approval must keep at least one line item. Nothing changes (the chain is not reset).

item.name: Add a second item to the pending claim -> 201

exec: pm.test("Two items, total 65.00", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(2); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("65.00"); });

request.description: Allowed, because another item remains.

exec: pm.test("One item left, total 25.00", function () { const c = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(c.lineItems.length).to.eql(1); pm.expect(c.total).to.eql("25.00"); });

pm.test("Reports each bad field with its path", function () { const paths = pm.response.json().error.details.map(d => d.path); ["lineItems.0.date","lineItems.0.category","lineItems.0.amount","lineItems.0.description"].forEach(p => pm.expect(paths).to.include(p)); });

request.description: A trailing comma is not valid JSON.

item.name: Claim id that is not a UUID -> 400

request.description: Needs 'Login as second claimant'. Refused in the query itself: 404, not 403.
Needs 'Login as approver'.

item.name: Update the claim with an empty body -> 400

request.description: The status follows the workflow; a client can never set it.
Out-of-scope claims look like they do not exist (404, not 403).

item.name: Submit with an id that is not a UUID -> 400
Update a field that cannot be edited (claimId) -> 400
